title: What It Means to Become a Person
coreMove: Loosen the need for a polished fixed self and choose the next more congruent act.
sourcePressure: Rogers treats becoming a person as an ongoing process of less defensive living and more open contact with experience, not a finished identity. Frozen sidecar ch06 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing becoming to self-help identity slogans or unfiltered expression.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of becoming
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
